title: Serve Performance Portrait: quantile panels + I/O-mode demux
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Build a consolidated dashboard that surfaces end-to-end serve performance quantiles (p50/p95/p99) broken down by model and API route, with a clear demultiplex between streaming and non-streaming I/O modes. The board should enable rapid triage: identify regression cohorts, pivot into traces, and correlate errors and retries. This ticket implements the dashboard panels, end-to-end query patterns, and the trace-linking hooks required for drilldown.
rationale: Our on-call and SRE teams currently jump between multiple boards when investigating degraded user experience for different interaction modes. A single pane that explicitly shows quantiles by model and route and separates streaming vs non-streaming will reduce mean time to identify root causes and speed rollbacks or fallbacks when a variant degrades.
technical_design: Data sources: metrics from Prometheus (serve.path.duration histograms + summary), traces from Jaeger-compatible tracing, logs from Loki for enriched error context.
Primary dimension keys: model_name, route, io_mode (streaming|blocking), model_variant, region, release_tag.
Quantile computation: use the summary-derived p50/p95/p99 where available; synthesize t-digest on ingest for histograms for accurate percentile aggregation where summaries are missing.

Panels: overview heatmap (models x routes) for p95; per-route time series for p50/p95/p99; stacked breakdown showing streaming vs non-streaming contribution; error-rate overlay and retry-rate small multiples.
Trace hooks: include a dashboard link template that attaches trace_id and request_id to deep-link into traces; implement consistent trace_id propagation in the SDK if missing (GH PR below).
Metrics pipeline changes: add a Prometheus scrape config for servepath_summary and ensure histogram buckets align with t-digest aggregation in the metrics ingestion job (metrics-team change).
Alerting: SLO-based alert rules for when p95 exceeds route-specific thresholds; anomaly detection via Holt-Winters baseline on p95 per-model-route.
Security & access: dashboard read rights default to infra+eng with a read-only link for PMs; no sensitive PII in queries (redact user identifiers in logs).
acceptance_criteria: A single dashboard in Console under 'Serve Performance' with overview + per-route detail exists and is linked from the runbook.
Panels show p50/p95/p99 for each model x route cell and clearly label streaming vs non-streaming contributions.
Clicking a cell opens a per-route view with time range selector and a 'Drill to trace' link that navigates to the trace viewer with trace_id prefilled.
Queries run within performance budget (panel queries < 2s typical) for 30d lookback on aggregate prod ingestion.
SLO alerts fire in test (staging) when synthetic traffic intentionally increases p95 beyond threshold and notifications include the dashboard link and top affected model/route.
Documentation updated: README with query examples and Owner/Runbook entries added to Confluence page linked in artifacts.
Design review signoff for visual approach from Marisol Vega (Design).
metrics_queries: PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serve_path_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_name, route, io_mode))
Log query (Loki): {job="serve", route=~"/v[0-9]+/.*"} |= "error" | json | topk(20, model_name)
Trace link template: https://traces.internal.redwood.com/trace/{{trace_id}}?from=dash> (constructed from dashboard panel variables)
Synthetic SLO test: run synthetic suite that creates 1k reqs/min for target route and assert p95 breach triggers alert in staging.
testing_plan: Unit tests for new query helpers in observability lib (tdigest aggregation).
End-to-end smoke: create synthetic streaming and blocking requests in staging; validate panels and trace links resolve to traces with the expected trace_id.
Performance test: run dashboard query load test to ensure panels return in <2s for 30d default range.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy metrics pipeline changes to staging and run synthetic test.
2) Create dashboard in staging and get signoff from SRE and Design.
3) Push dashboard to production during low-traffic maintenance window and monitor query latency for 24h.
4) Post-deploy: 1-week observation; if p95 query latency exceeds 2s or incorrect aggregates observed, rollback and open follow-up ticket.
